answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity stake a refundable bond before it can forge transactions or access shared services. A new agent starts with a small trust limit, and its bond is slashed when peers prove fraud, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Honest agents gradually earn a higher limit, turning the network into a haven for reputable actors, while a nebula of cheap sock-puppet accounts stays quarantined at the edge, unable to reach valuable work until it has proven itself over time.
